findings.title: retryCount cleanup clause is not limited to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch, `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. The first branch is SMS-only, and the comment says this handler deletes SMS reminders. `WorkflowReminder` is shared with EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. Today only this cron increments `retryCount`, so nothing is wrongly deleted yet. If another cron (email or WhatsApp) later uses the column, this SMS cron will delete its reminders as well. Scope the clause to `method: SMS`, or use `AND` with the method.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update inside catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (DB error, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, giving a Prisma 'record not found'), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler then fails with a 500, and every remaining reminder in that run is skipped. Before this change, per-reminder errors were only logged and the loop continued. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log first and then update safely.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient number or empty message are never counted as failures
findings.body: `retryCount` is only incremented when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing (for example an attendee with no `smsReminderNumber`), the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` block is skipped and nothing is recorded. Those reminders stay `scheduled: false` and are re-processed on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes. That is the same endless-retry behaviour the PR sets out to remove. An invalid or missing phone number is the PR's own example. Add an `else` that increments `retryCount` for this case too.

findings.title: Two attempts is a very aggressive threshold for transient failures, and the counter is a stale read-modify-write
findings.body: All failures count the same, including transient Twilio or network errors. Because the cron runs often, a short outage can burn both attempts and permanently delete a valid reminder (`retryCount > 1`). The increment is also computed from the value read at the start of the run (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) rather than an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`. If two cron invocations overlap, both write the same value and the counter under-counts. Use `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, and consider a larger limit or distinguishing permanent errors (such as an invalid number) from transient ones.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes the cron's deletion criteria and adds retry bookkeeping in both the failure and exception paths. It adds no tests for incrementing on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result or on a thrown error, deleting once `retryCount > 1`, or leaving non-SMS reminders untouched.
